Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'duo_pose' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'pose': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'duo_hinge' reports the pose, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the pose and angle with 'duo_hinge'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'duo_pose' and take a 'screenshot'; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator this session already uses, else a booted one no other session is using, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

pose.description: For 'duo_pose': the pose to move the hinge to.

angle.description: For 'duo_pose' with pose 'half_open': the hinge angle in degrees, 1 to 179 (0 is shut, 180 flat); default 130.

tools.name: mcp__computer-use__app_ax_find
tools.description:
Search the accessibility elements captured by the last app_screenshot of one window. Filter by role (e.g. "AXTextArea", "AXButton") and/or title substring. Returns matching elements with their [N] index — pass that as element_index to app_click/app_type. Use this when the inline summary in app_screenshot doesn't show the element you need (it only lists the first few actionable ones).

This tool acts on one application in the BACKGROUND while the user keeps working in other apps. The target window does not come to the front. For the menu bar use app_menu. `app` says which application a call acts on. To act in another granted application, call the app_* tools with that application; no release is needed in between. tools.name: mcp__computer-use__computer_batch

Use this whenever you can predict the outcome of several actions ahead — e.g. click a field, type into it, press Return. Actions execute sequentially and stop on the first error. The frontmost application must be in the session allowlist at the time of this call, or this tool returns an error and does nothing. The frontmost check runs before EACH action inside the batch — if an action opens a non-allowed app, the next action's gate fires and the batch stops there. Screenshot and zoom actions are allowed and their images are returned interleaved with the per-action outputs. Coordinates you write in THIS batch — clicks AND zoom regions — always refer to the full-screen screenshot taken BEFORE this call, never to a zoom and never to a mid-batch screenshot. After the batch returns, the most recent full screenshot it produced becomes the new coordinate reference for your next call. In this session the tools that each carry out one of this tool's actions (left_click, type, key, scroll, left_click_drag, screenshot, etc.) are not available on their own: a single action is a one-item batch. entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_bring_to_current_space

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_click
entries.description:

For a web page's dropdown the refusal says how to choose an option without opening it. entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_key
entries.description:

Otherwise — and always for tab, shift+tab, the arrow keys up/down/left/right (alone or with shift, cmd or option), home, end, pageup and pagedown — the key goes as a keystroke to whatever has keyboard focus in that window, so app_click the field or list first and check the effect with app_screenshot. Use app_menu for ⌘-shortcuts. A native app in the background ignores a cmd+a keystroke, so it is refused there. To overwrite all the text of ONE text box or shape on a Keynote-style canvas, double-click into it, press cmd+up, then shift+cmd+down, then app_type. Use those two keys only while such a box is being edited: in a document body (Pages, TextEdit) they select the WHOLE document, and in a list or on a selected table cell they do other things. Press escape once; another with nothing left to cancel only plays the Mac's alert sound.

entries.description:

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__computer_batch
entries.description: Execute a sequence of actions in ONE tool call. Each individual tool call requires a model→API round trip (seconds); batching a predictable sequence eliminates all but one. The frontmost application must be in the session allowlist at the time of this call, or this tool returns an error and does nothing. The frontmost check runs before EACH action inside the batch — if an action opens a non-allowed app, the next action's gate fires and the batch stops there. Screenshot and zoom actions are allowed and their images are returned interleaved with the per-action outputs. Coordinates you write in THIS batch — clicks AND zoom regions — always refer to the full-screen screenshot taken BEFORE this call, never to a zoom and never to a mid-batch screenshot. After the batch returns, the most recent full screenshot it produced becomes the new coordinate reference for your next call. In this session the tools that each carry out one of this tool's actions (left_click, type, key, scroll, left_click_drag, screenshot, etc.) are not available on their own: a single action is a one-item batch. The app_* tools (app_screenshot, app_click, app_type, app_key, app_batch, etc.) act on granted applications without taking over the screen.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__teach_batch
entries.description: Queue multiple teach steps in one tool call. Parallels computer_batch: N steps → one model↔API round trip instead of N. Each step still shows a tooltip and waits for the user's Next click, but YOU aren't waiting for a round trip between steps. You can call teach_batch multiple times in one tour — treat each batch as one predictable SEGMENT (typically: all the steps on one page). Returns {exited:true, stepsCompleted:N} if the user clicks Exit — do NOT call again after that; {stepsCompleted, stepFailed, ...} if an action errors mid-batch; otherwise {stepsCompleted, results:[...]} plus a final screenshot. Fall back to individual teach_step calls when you need to react to each intermediate screenshot.

---
name: drive-app-with-posted-key-events
description: "Drive the built JusPrin app headlessly (even with the screen locked) by posting CGEvents to its pid with a tiny Swift tool; keys work, mouse clicks do not, and the send dialog is reachable by keyboard."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6b96dccc-1cb4-4f72-9de4-3ecee4b28e74
  modified: 2026-09-08T05:58:16.222Z
---

When the Mac screen is locked (`ioreg -n Root -d1 | grep CGSSessionScreenIsLocked`), the computer-use MCP request is auto-denied, `screencapture` fails, and System Events sees zero windows. Key events still reach the app: a 15-line Swift program calling `CGEvent(keyboardEventSource:virtualKey:keyDown:).postToPid(pid)` (compile with `swiftc`) made the app slice on Cmd+R (keycode 15) and open the send dialog on Cmd+Shift+G (keycode 5). Mouse events posted the same way did nothing, even with the window number set on the event.

Inside `PrintHostSendDialog` (Orca `MsgDialog`), focus starts in the filename field; Tab (48) moves to the "Upload" button, Right (124) to "Upload and Print", Space (49) presses it, because Orca's custom `Button` handles Space/Return and arrow navigation itself. Return alone triggers plain "Upload" (the affirmative id), not print.

`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` still lists the app's on-screen windows with bounds while locked, which tells you when a modal dialog is open (a small layer-0 window appears) and when it closed.

**Why:** On 2026-09-07 the end-to-end proof of the fake Moonraker printer needed the Print button pressed while the screen was locked; this was the only working path.

**How to apply:** Confirm the target pid first (`pgrep -f <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS`) so keys never go to another session's instance. Watch the app's own `--datadir` `log/debug_*.log` for effects (use `/usr/bin/grep -a`; the default `grep` is ugrep, which treats `\|` literally and may skip the log as binary). See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]].
